title: xBS-GNN: Accelerating Billion-Scale GNNTraining on FPGA
problem: GNN training on billion-scale graphs incurs high volume of irregular data accessing, and existing accelerators cannot scale to such large graphs due to memory capacity limitations on conventional hardware.
motivation: GNNs are widely used in important applications like Electronic Design Automation and molecular property prediction, but training on large-scale graphs with billions of edges is prohibitively time-consuming.
method: The system uses three techniques to fit billion-scale graph training into FPGA memory. It arranges data to match the neural network's access pattern for faster retrieval, uses compact lookup tables so vertices need only small index numbers instead of full identifiers, and reduces number precision to shrink data size. Combined, these reduce memory use enough to train billion-node graphs in FPGA memory at full speed.
key_novelty: The core idea is combining data arrangement, vertex renaming (giving nodes shorter names for smaller storage), and precision reduction so billion-scale graphs fit in FPGA memory during training.
contributions: Novel data placement policy optimized for GNN training access patterns
Vertex-renaming technique with memory-efficient lookup table design for fast data retrieval
Feature quantization mechanism to reduce memory traffic
FPGA-based system architecture demonstrating scalability on multi-FPGA platforms with 8.39× speedup over GPU baseline

metrics.speedup: 8.39× over GPU baseline, 5.13× over state-of-the-art GNN accelerator

primary_theme: FPGA acceleration for billion-scale GNN training
